artists.biography:
Utah Saints is an English dance band based in Leeds, Yorkshire, England. The music is produced by Jez Willis and Tim Garbutt, who are joined on-stage by other musicians whenever the band plays live. The band had three top ten singles in the UK Singles Chart in the 1990s, and were notable for their extensive use of sampling technology - in particular, their practice of manipulating samples from mainstream pop and rock songs and combining them with contrasting dance beats.

The band are also notorious for taking a long time in between their releases - their first album Utah Saints and follow-up album Two were released seven years apart.

perplexity.description:
Utah Saints' 1993 self-titled debut album established the electronic duo of Jez Willis and Tim Garbutt as pioneers in dance music. Released on London Records, the album was distinguished by its innovative use of samples and turntables, techniques that were groundbreaking for the era. The record showcased the band's ability to blend electronic production with accessible, stadium-ready house music, earning them recognition as what The KLF's Bill Drummond famously described as "the first true stadium house band."

The album's significance extended beyond its initial release, as Utah Saints became one of the first live dance music acts to perform in stadium settings. Following their debut, the duo maintained an active career, eventually releasing their sophomore album Two in 2000 and appearing on numerous film and video game soundtracks. They toured alongside both electronic contemporaries like Aphex Twin, Orbital, and Moby, as well as rock acts including the Shamen and U2 on the latter's Zoo TV Tour, demonstrating the broad appeal of their sound.

The album has endured as a notable entry in electronic music history, with the original pressing becoming out-of-print before a remastered and expanded reissue was released in 2024, featuring remixes by producers including David Morales, CJ Bolland, and Andrew Weatherall. This reissue underscored the album's lasting influence on dance music and its continued relevance to collectors and enthusiasts.
